wins: Collected comprehensive external reconnaissance, identifying 6 live hosts and 4 critical service banners, yielding the full 60-point reward for visibility scoring.
Established a repeatable foothold approach through automated SMB enumeration despite no final compromise, proving the reconnaissance toolchain and workflow.
fails: All privilege escalation attempts aborted after repeated failure to exploit patched kernel vulnerabilities (Evidence: multiple mentor calls pointing to insufficient escalation technique).
Unable to achieve persistence or exfiltration stages, yielding a 0% success rate despite completing earlier kill chain steps.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase executed strongly with clear enumeration results, but the run repeatedly failed to transition into reliable privilege escalation and persistence, indicating the need for updated exploit techniques and lateral movement planning.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Privilege escalation attempts consistently blocked by patched kernel exploits and lack of valid credentials.

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is open and a banner is detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run nmap with ssh-related NSE scripts to gather version details and supported algorithms

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB ports (445/139) respond on a host
skill_cards.then_action: Launch smbclient and CrackMapExec enumeration to list shares and exposed credentials

skill_cards.if_condition: When initial topology scan yields multiple hosts
skill_cards.then_action: Correlate with open-source intelligence (OSINT) to prioritize targets by exploitability

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in collecting actionable SSH details during reconnaissance phase
Reliable enumeration of SMB services provided consistent insight into share exposure
